decisions.reason: As a newly launched adjacent product line with several models and its own page, it preserves a low-cost growth option in consumer health for an expanding large firm, so it is likely to be kept while demand becomes clearer.

This hair-and-skin supplement fits the firm's portfolio-broadening strategy and pharmacy channels, and after only a short time on the market the uncertainty is still worth carrying at relatively low cost.

Joint-health supplements are close to the firm's established offer and the early signal is not negative, so real-options logic favors keeping it on the market until sales evidence is more informative.

The mushroom-based immune supplement is more niche and thus more uncertain, but because it is still adjacent to the consumer-health offer and likely inexpensive to maintain, the firm would probably keep the option open for now.

The documented Valsartan problem is a strong negative signal in a highly regulated category, and for a large portfolio firm the quality, regulatory, and reputational costs make abandonment within the next year more likely than continued support.
